'''Harry Paul''' (born 11 February 1931) is a German theoretical physicist at the [[Humboldt University of Berlin]], where he is emeritus professor of physics. His research areas include laser physics, [[nonlinear optics]], and [[quantum optics]].<ref name=gebu>{{Cite web |date=2011 |title=Zum 80. Geburtstag von Harry Paul |first=Ulf |last=Leonhardt |first2=Wolfgang |last2=Schleich |journal=Physik Journal |url=https://pro-physik.de/zeitschriften/download/15167}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Paul was born to a [[Sudeten Germans|Sudeten German]] family in [[Czechoslovakia]]. In the summer of 1945, he and his family resettled in Germany. Beginning in 1949, he studied physics at the [[University of Rostock]] and the University of Jena. After earning his diploma in 1955, he joined the Institute for Theoretical Physics at the [[University of Jena]] as an assistant. He received his doctorate in 1958 and subsequently worked as a research scientist at the [[Academy of Sciences of the GDR]]. Since 1962, he worked under Gustav Richter at the Central Institute for Optics and Spectroscopy (''Zentralinstitut für Optik und Spektroskopie'') in Berlin, which later became the [[Ferdinand-Braun-Institut]]. In 1964, Paul completed his habilitation at the [[Humboldt University of Berlin]]. Until 1969, he worked at the Institute for Special Problems of Theoretical Physics, [[Academy of Sciences of the GDR]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Brunner |first=W. |last2=Fischer |first2=R. |last3=Paul |first3=H. |date=1985 |title=Regular and chaotic behavior of multimode lasers |url=https://opg.optica.org/abstract.cfm?URI=josab-2-1-202 |journal=Journal of the Optical Society of America B |language=en |volume=2 |issue=1 |pages=202 |doi=10.1364/JOSAB.2.000202 |issn=0740-3224|url-access=subscription }}</ref> In 1978, Paul was appointed as a professor at the [[Humboldt University of Berlin]].<ref name=gebu />

Following [[German reunification]], he became head of the Nonclassical Radiation research group of the [[Max Planck Society]] at [[Humboldt University of Berlin]] in 1992. In 1993, he was appointed Professor of Theoretical Physics at the same institution, where he remained until his retirement in 1996.<ref name=fm>{{Cite book |last=Paul |first=Harry |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/product/identifier/9780511616754/type/book |title=Introduction to Quantum Optics: From Light Quanta to Quantum Teleportation |date=2004 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-0-521-83563-3 |edition=1 |translator-last=Jex |translator-first=Igor |doi=10.1017/cbo9780511616754}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
In 1980, together with Witlof Brunner, he was awarded the [[National Prize of the GDR]] (Third Class) for Science and Technology for their contributions to [[Quantum optics|quantum electronic]]s.<ref>{{Cite web |title=DFG-Viewer: Neues Deutschland |url=https://dfg-viewer.de/show/?set%5Bmets%5D=https://content.staatsbibliothek-berlin.de/zefys/SNP2532889X-19801008-0-0-0-0.xml&tx_dlf%5Bpage%5D=4 |website=dfg-viewer.de}}</ref> In 1999, he was elected a full member of the Natural Sciences Class of the Sudeten German Academy of Sciences and Arts.<ref name=gebu />
